name: Wikimedia Analytics API (Pageviews and Unique Devices)
summary: Free page-view, top-article and unique-device statistics for Wikipedia and sibling Wikimedia projects.
description: The Analytics Query Service serves per-article page views (daily or monthly), project-wide aggregates, most-viewed article rankings per day or month, and unique-device counts for every Wikimedia project. It is a separate host and API from the content REST API in wikipedia-api (wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/metrics versus en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1). The docs also cover edits, editors, bytes changed and media-file metrics. At check, daily data for 2026-10 was available.

required_headers.name: User-Agent
required_headers.notes: The docs require an identifying User-Agent; a request with an empty User-Agent returned 403.

rate_limit.summary: No numbers on the Analytics API pages; limits depend on client identity (see the Wikimedia API rate-limit policy). Wait for each request to finish before sending the next.

endpoints.summary: Views of one article, daily or monthly
Total views for a whole project
Most-viewed articles for a month or day (day=all-days for a month)

coverage.geographic: All Wikimedia projects (for example en.wikipedia, de.wikipedia, commons.wikimedia)
coverage.temporal: Daily and monthly series up to the previous day or month; 2026-10 daily data present at check

agent_notes: Project is the hostname without the scheme (en.wikipedia, not en.wikipedia.org, for per-article; the docs example for aggregate uses en.wikipedia.org). Article titles use underscores and must be URL-encoded. Timestamps are YYYYMMDD or YYYYMMDDHH. Use agent=user to exclude spiders and automated traffic; the access and agent values used in the docs and checks were all-access and user. Top lists include Main_Page and Special:Search, so filter them out.
caveats: A valid but unknown article or a date range with no data returns 404 with a JSON error body, not an empty list.
Rate limits are not numbered in the API docs; Wikimedia may block clients that ignore its User-Agent policy.
The spec at wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/?spec is a generic one and was not checked for the metrics endpoints, so no OpenAPI link is given.

verification.notes: Exact example executed without credentials; per-article, aggregate, top and unique-devices endpoints all returned 200.
